# JohnB.io

> A personal AI and development project site by John Bowman. Built to test, explore and showcase 28 free AI-powered tools, a 35-lesson AI & machine learning course, responsible AI frameworks, and developer utilities.

## Pages

- [Home](https://johnb.io/): Projects gallery — browse all 28 free AI tools, developer utilities and projects on the site.
- [About](https://johnb.io/about): John Bowman, AI strategist and developer based in Leeds. 20+ years in iGaming and digital marketing, University of Oxford AI Programme graduate (2024), builds the free AI tools on JohnB.io.
- [Contact](https://johnb.io/contact): Get in touch via email or LinkedIn. Also handles GDPR data privacy requests.
- [Privacy Policy](https://johnb.io/privacy): How JohnB.io handles analytics, tool inputs and GDPR data rights.
- [Terms of Use](https://johnb.io/terms): Terms and conditions governing use of the free tools and course on JohnB.io.

## AI Tools

- [Search & Prompt Radar](https://johnb.io/search-radar): Free keyword and prompt research tool. Enter a seed topic and region (UK, US or global) and it pulls live autocomplete suggestions from Google Search and YouTube, Reddit search intent, recent Hacker News threads and LinkedIn B2B modifiers, then turns them into likely ChatGPT, Perplexity and Claude prompts (synthesised by Claude Haiku 5.5, not scraped) and LinkedIn post hooks. One-click copy, Markdown copy for LLM workflows and CSV export.
- [AI Meditation Generator](https://johnb.io/meditation): Generates personalised guided meditations with Claude Sonnet 5.5 scripts, OpenAI TTS narration (Shimmer, Onyx or Nova voice) and 10 browser-synthesised soundscapes including ocean, fire crackle and binaural tones. Choose 5, 10 or 20 minutes in 25 languages including Spanish, French, German, Japanese and Arabic. Downloadable as MP3. Not medical advice.
- [Live Poker Hand Replayer](https://johnb.io/live-poker-hand-replayer): Turn any live No Limit Hold'em poker hand into an animated table replay. Build the hand in a guided form or paste notes parsed by Claude Haiku 5.5, add optional OpenAI TTS commentary, then share a link or embed the replay anywhere.
- [AI CV Enhancer](https://johnb.io/aitocv): Upload a CV (PDF, DOCX or text) and job description to get a tailored CV, cover letter, suitability match score and interview prep powered by Claude Sonnet 5.5 in 9 language variants (English, Italian, Spanish, French, Brazilian Portuguese, European Portuguese, Romanian, German and Bulgarian), plus integrated job board search across 9 countries and iGaming specialist boards. Also accessible via aitocv.com.
- [AI Copyeditor](https://johnb.io/editor): Paste or upload text/Word documents to get AI-powered copyediting powered by Claude Sonnet 5.5 with UK/US English support, custom brand style guide rules and excluded words.
- [Gen Z Translator](https://johnb.io/genz): AI-powered translator using Claude Haiku 5.5 that rewrites plain English into Gen Z slang and translates Gen Z slang back into plain English.
- [LLM Chat](https://johnb.io/lm-chat): Side-by-side chat interface comparing Anthropic Claude, OpenAI GPT and Google Gemini responses to the same prompt in real time.
- [YouTube Blog Post Generator](https://johnb.io/transcripts): Paste a YouTube video URL or transcript and get a structured, SEO-optimised blog post generated by Claude Haiku 5.5.
- [Text to Speech Converter](https://johnb.io/text-to-speech): Convert text to natural-sounding speech and download as MP3. Powered by OpenAI TTS (tts-1 model) with six voice options (Alloy, Echo, Fable, Onyx, Nova, Shimmer) and adjustable playback speed. Up to 4,000 characters per conversion.
- [Football 2026](https://johnb.io/football-2026): AI predictions for the Summer 2026 football tournament. Group stage results, interactive knockout bracket, squad ratings and win probability for all 48 teams. Click to change bracket winners.
- [Recipe to Shopping List](https://johnb.io/recipe-shopping-list): Paste a recipe or a week's meal plan and get one consolidated UK supermarket shopping list powered by Claude Haiku 5.5, deduped across recipes with quantities summed and grouped by aisle. American ingredient names are translated to UK retail terms. Each item links to a pre-filled product search at Tesco, Sainsbury's, Asda, Morrisons, Ocado, Waitrose, Iceland or Co-op.

## Developer Tools

- [iGaming Bonus Cost Calculator](https://johnb.io/bonus-calculator): Model the true cost of casino bonus offers. Enter bonus amount, wagering requirement, house edge and player completion rate to calculate net operator cost per bonus issued, breakeven house edge, and a scenario table across five completion rates.
- [iGaming RG Message Generator](https://johnb.io/rg-generator): Generate compliant responsible gambling disclaimers for 10 jurisdictions including UK (UKGC), Malta (MGA), Ontario, Netherlands, Sweden, Denmark, Germany, Ireland, Spain and Gibraltar. Provides copy-paste disclaimer text, required logos and seals, helpline details, self-exclusion scheme information and channel-specific guidance for email, display, social media and SMS.
- [iGaming Regulatory Compliance Map](https://johnb.io/igaming-compliance): Interactive world map of 212 iGaming regulations across 50 jurisdictions. Browse gambling laws, AML directives, data protection rules and advertising codes by country — filterable by region and category.
- [iGaming Regulations Dataset (JSON)](https://johnb.io/igaming-regulations.json): Machine-readable export of all 212 iGaming regulations across 50 jurisdictions, licensed CC BY 4.0. Each record carries the regulation name, category, region, jurisdiction codes and names, a hand-written summary and a link to the official regulator source. Individual jurisdictions are citable on the map at https://johnb.io/igaming-compliance#jurisdiction-united-kingdom and individual regulations at #reg-<id>.
- [PDF Merger](https://johnb.io/pdf-merger): Merge multiple PDF files into one instantly using pdf-lib in the browser. Upload, preview, reorder and download your combined PDF — no server upload and no file size limits.
- [eBay & Vinted Profit Calculator](https://johnb.io/ebay): Calculate net profit from eBay, Vinted and auction sales, accounting for platform fees, postage and purchase costs.
- [Bill Calculator](https://johnb.io/calculator): Split bills and calculate tips per person. Built with Python running in the browser via Pyodide.
- [Poker Bankroll Planner](https://johnb.io/bankroll): Evaluate poker experience level and plan bankroll and stake strategy.
- [Text to Voice](https://johnb.io/text-to-voice): Browser-based text-to-speech using the Web Speech API with voice selection, speed control and word-by-word subtitle highlighting.
- [Zig-Zag Drop Mystery](https://johnb.io/zzmystery): Interactive browser pachinko and plinko slot drop game demo with configurable ball drops, multipliers and mystery prize mechanics.

## Digital AI Tools

- [T&Cs Simplifier](https://johnb.io/tcs-simplifier): Paste casino bonus terms and conditions and get a plain English summary, red flag list and key numbers block (wagering, expiry, max bet, max win) powered by Claude Haiku 5.5. Built for players, affiliates and compliance teams. Not legal advice.
- [Prompt Improver](https://johnb.io/prompt-improver): Rewrites weak AI prompts into stronger versions with a short change log using Claude Haiku 5.5. Includes a library of starter prompts for common tasks (summarising, cold email, code review, SEO briefs, meeting notes). Works for ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and any LLM.
- [FAQ Schema Generator](https://johnb.io/faq-schema): Free tool that turns question and answer pairs into valid FAQPage JSON-LD structured data. Includes a manual builder and an AI draft mode powered by Claude Haiku 5.5 that generates 5–8 FAQs from a topic. Output is ready to paste into the page head.
- [Content Repurposer](https://johnb.io/content-repurposer): AI-powered tool using Claude Haiku 5.5 that repurposes existing content into six formats simultaneously — LinkedIn posts, X threads, Facebook posts, email newsletters, and 10s/30s video scripts.
- [iGaming Promo Copy Generator](https://johnb.io/promo-copy): Generate compliant iGaming promotional copy for 10 regulated markets including UK (UKGC), Malta (MGA), Ontario, Netherlands, Germany and more using Claude Haiku 5.5. Describe a promotion, select jurisdiction, channel and tone, and receive AI-generated headlines, body copy, call-to-action text, T&C summaries and market-specific required disclaimers.
- [iGaming Jargon Translator](https://johnb.io/igaming-jargon): AI-powered tool using Claude Haiku 5.5 that translates iGaming industry terminology to plain English, or plain English descriptions to correct industry terminology. Covers GGR, NGR, RTP, wagering requirements, KYC/AML, CPA, RevShare, CLV, responsible gambling frameworks and more.
- [LLMs.txt Generator](https://johnb.io/llms-generator): AI-powered tool using Claude Haiku 5.5 that generates a structured llms.txt file from a URL or pasted content. Helps websites become more discoverable and accurately cited by AI assistants including ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Perplexity. Follows the llmstxt.org specification.

## AI Course

- [AI & Machine Learning Course](https://johnb.io/course/): Free AI and machine learning course with certificate. 9 units and 35 lessons covering AI fundamentals, deep learning, NLP, MLOps and business strategy. No login required to browse lessons.
- [Certificate Verification](https://johnb.io/verify): Public page to verify AI & Machine Learning Course certificates issued by JohnB.io. URL format: johnb.io/verify/JB-2026-XXXXXX

### Unit 1 — Introduction to AI
- [What Is AI? History, Definitions and the Turing Test](https://johnb.io/course/what-is-ai): Covers AI history from the 1950s, Alan Turing's 1950 test, AI winters, and why modern AI is pattern matching at scale.
- [Categories of AI: Narrow, General and Super AI](https://johnb.io/course/categories-of-ai): Explains the three tiers of AI capability — narrow AI (what exists today), AGI (theoretical), and ASI (hypothetical).
- [How AI Learns: Supervised, Unsupervised and Reinforcement Learning](https://johnb.io/course/how-ai-learns): The three core learning paradigms that power modern AI systems.
- [AI vs Augmented Intelligence](https://johnb.io/course/ai-vs-augmented-intelligence): Explores the distinction between AI replacing humans and AI enhancing human decision-making.

### Unit 2 — AI Landscape
- [Traditional AI vs Generative AI](https://johnb.io/course/traditional-vs-generative-ai): How rules-based and statistical AI differs from modern generative models.
- [ML, Deep Learning and Neural Networks](https://johnb.io/course/ml-deep-learning-neural-networks): The relationship between machine learning, deep learning and neural networks explained clearly.
- [Key AI Subfields](https://johnb.io/course/key-ai-subfields): NLP, computer vision, robotics, and other major branches of AI.
- [AI Tools and Platforms in 2026](https://johnb.io/course/ai-tools-platforms-2026): Overview of the leading AI tools, foundation models and platforms available to practitioners in 2026.

### Unit 3 — AI Ethics and Governance
- [AI Failures and Ethics](https://johnb.io/course/ai-failures-ethics): Real-world AI failures and the ethical lessons they teach.
- [Hallucinations, Bias and IP](https://johnb.io/course/ai-hallucinations-bias-ip): Why AI systems hallucinate, how bias enters models, and intellectual property considerations.
- [AI Governance Frameworks](https://johnb.io/course/ai-governance-frameworks): How organisations and regulators are approaching AI governance, including the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF and ISO/IEC 42001.

### Unit 4 — Python for AI

### Unit 5 — Machine Learning Fundamentals

- [Backpropagation](https://johnb.io/course/backpropagation): How neural networks learn by propagating error signals backwards through layers.
- [Activation Functions and the Vanishing Gradient](https://johnb.io/course/activation-functions-vanishing-gradient): ReLU, sigmoid, tanh and why the vanishing gradient problem matters.

# Extended Tool Reference & FAQs (llms-full.txt)

Below is the complete structured reference for all 28 interactive tools on JohnB.io, including how each tool works and its frequently asked questions.

## AI CV Enhancer: Tailored CV & Cover Letter
- **URL**: https://johnb.io/aitocv
- **Summary**: Upload your CV and a job description. Get a tailored CV, cover letter, suitability score and interview prep powered by Claude AI.

### How It Works
1. Upload your CV by dropping a PDF, DOCX or TXT file onto the upload area, or paste the text directly into the input field below it.
2. Paste the job description into the right-hand panel. The more detail the job listing includes - responsibilities, required skills, company context - the more precisely the tool can tailor your CV. Leave the output language on Same as the job description, or pick one of nine languages.
3. Click Enhance My CV & Write Cover Letter. Claude Sonnet analyses both documents, rewrites your CV to highlight the most relevant experience, and generates a personalised cover letter for the role.
4. Review your results. You will receive a tailored CV, a cover letter, a suitability score out of 10, a list of any skills gaps to address, and a set of likely interview questions with suggested answers.
5. Download your documents as Word or PDF files. Use the role-fit finder to discover other roles that suit your background, and the job board search to apply directly.

### Frequently Asked Questions
- **Q: Which AI model does this tool use?**
  A: The tool uses Claude Sonnet by Anthropic - specifically Claude Sonnet 5.5 ( claude-sonnet-5-5 ). Sonnet is a more capable model than Claude Haiku and was chosen here because tailoring professional documents to specific roles requires stronger reasoning and instruction-following than simpler tasks.
- **Q: Is my CV stored or shared?**
  A: No. Your CV and job description are sent to Anthropic's API to process your request only. Anthropic does not use API inputs to train its models by default, and JohnB.io does not log, store or share the content you submit. See the Anthropic Privacy Policy for full details. Do not include highly sensitive personal information such as passport numbers, national insurance numbers or financial details.
- **Q: What file formats can I upload?**
  A: The tool accepts PDF, DOCX and TXT files. PDF and DOCX are recommended for preserving formatting. The text content is extracted on upload - embedded images and complex tables may not transfer perfectly, so check the extracted text before submitting.
- **Q: Can it write my CV in another language?**
  A: Yes. Choose an output language under the job description: English, Italian, Spanish, French, Portuguese (Brazil or Portugal), Romanian, German or Bulgarian. The default, Same as the job description, matches the language the job advert is written in, so a Spanish advert gets a Spanish CV, cover letter and interview prep. Company names and qualification titles are kept as they are, and the PDF download supports accented letters and Cyrillic.
- **Q: How good is the tailored CV at beating ATS screening?**
  A: The output is designed to incorporate relevant keywords from the job description in a natural way, which improves ATS pass rates. However, every employer configures their ATS differently. Tools like Jobscan can give you a more precise match score for a specific ATS. Use the AI output as a strong starting point, then review it yourself before applying.
- **Q: What is the daily usage limit?**
  A: The tool allows up to 20 enhancements per day per user. This limit applies per IP address and resets at midnight UTC. If you need higher-volume access, get in touch via LinkedIn .

## Search & Prompt Radar - Keyword & AI Prompt Tool
- **URL**: https://johnb.io/search-radar
- **Summary**: Free keyword and AI prompt research tool. Scan Google, YouTube, Reddit and LinkedIn demand for any topic, plus likely ChatGPT prompts for AEO and GEO.

### How It Works
1. Enter a seed. A product, tool, problem or topic between 2 and 80 characters, such as n8n automation.
2. Pick a region. UK, US or Global. It changes the country hint sent to Google and YouTube.
3. Scan. The tool queries Google autocomplete, YouTube autocomplete and Hacker News in parallel, then shows which platforms answered and which didn't.
4. Synthesise prompts. The collected terms go to an AI model, which writes likely assistant prompts and groups the terms into intent clusters. If that step fails you get rule-based prompts, labelled as such.
5. Filter and copy. Narrow the results to Questions, Comparisons or Tutorials, and click any term, prompt or hook to copy it.
6. Export. Copy everything as Markdown to paste into an LLM, or download a CSV for a spreadsheet. The page URL updates too, so you can share the scan.

### Frequently Asked Questions
- **Q: Is Search & Prompt Radar free?**
  A: Yes. It's free and there's no sign-up. Each IP address gets 20 fresh scans a day, and repeating a scan that's already cached doesn't count towards that limit.
- **Q: Where does the data come from?**
  A: Google and YouTube autocomplete suggestions for your seed, Reddit search suggestions from Google, and Hacker News threads from the last 12 months. The LinkedIn card turns that demand into B2B angles, and the AI prompts card is synthesised from all of it. A repeat scan of the same seed can return a cached copy rather than fresh data.
- **Q: Are the ChatGPT prompts real?**
  A: They're not taken from ChatGPT. No AI platform publishes its prompt logs, so the prompts are synthesised from the real Google, YouTube, Reddit and Hacker News data the tool collects. Treat them as a reasoned estimate of what people ask AI assistants, grouped by Discovery, Comparison and Implementation intent.
- **Q: Why does the tool show Hacker News threads instead of Reddit threads?**
  A: Reddit now blocks anonymous access to its search data, so live Reddit threads can't be fetched without an approved API account. The tool still shows what people search for on Reddit, taken from Google autocomplete, and links straight to Reddit search. Live threads come from Hacker News, which works best for tech, AI and startup topics.
- **Q: Can I export the results?**
  A: Yes. Copy all for LLM copies every result as clean Markdown you can paste into ChatGPT, Claude or a content brief. Export CSV downloads a file with platform, category and term columns that opens in Excel or Google Sheets. You can also click any single term to copy it.
- **Q: What does the region setting change?**
  A: It sets the country Google and YouTube use for their suggestions, so UK returns British phrasing and spelling while US returns American queries. Global drops the country hint altogether. Hacker News is one site worldwide, so its threads don't change between regions.

## AI Meditation Generator - Personalised & Free
- **URL**: https://johnb.io/meditation
- **Summary**: Free AI meditation generator. Enter your name and goal, pick 5, 10 or 20 minutes and get a personalised guided meditation with voice and soundscape.

### How It Works
1. Fill in the form. Your first name is optional. Pick a goal or describe your own, choose 5, 10 or 20 minutes, then select a voice and a soundscape.
2. Claude writes your script. The AI writes a timed meditation built around your goal - short spoken passages with deliberate pauses between them, personalised with your name.
3. The voice is generated. Each passage is converted to speech by OpenAI text to speech at a slowed, calm pace. The first passage is ready within seconds; the rest load quietly in the background.
4. Press play. Your browser synthesises the soundscape live with the Web Audio API and plays each spoken passage at the right moment, gently lowering the music while the voice speaks.
5. Follow the voice. When the session ends the soundscape fades out slowly. Take a moment before you move. You can also download the finished session as an MP3, or share it straight to WhatsApp from your phone.

### Frequently Asked Questions
- **Q: What does the AI Meditation Generator do?**
  A: It creates a personalised guided meditation from three inputs: your name, what you want to work on and how long you have. Claude writes a script built around your goal, an AI voice reads it aloud, and a calming soundscape plays underneath. Every session is unique.
- **Q: Is it free?**
  A: Yes. You get 3 meditations per day at no cost. The limit exists because each session costs real money in AI usage. If you want more than 3 a day, get in touch on LinkedIn.
- **Q: Is this medical advice?**
  A: No. This is a relaxation aid, not a treatment for any medical condition, including high blood pressure, anxiety disorders or insomnia. If you have a health concern, speak to a doctor. Stop the session if you feel unwell.
- **Q: Do you store my name or goal?**
  A: No. Your name and goal are sent to a Cloudflare Worker, used to generate the script and audio, and never saved. The only thing stored is a rate-limit counter tied to your IP address, which expires within two days.
- **Q: Why does the voice pause between passages?**
  A: Guided meditation is mostly silence. The voice speaks for a few seconds, then leaves space for you to follow the instruction while the soundscape continues. Longer sessions use longer pauses, and sleep meditations use the longest of all.
- **Q: Can I listen with the screen locked?**
  A: Not reliably. The audio is generated and mixed live in your browser, and phones suspend browser audio when the screen locks. Keep the tab open and the screen on, or use a desktop. Headphones give the best experience.
- **Q: Can I download my meditation?**
  A: Yes. Once all the voice passages have loaded, use Download MP3 to save the full session with the voice and soundscape mixed at the background volume you set on the slider. On a phone, the Share button sends the file straight to WhatsApp or any other app.

## Recipe to Shopping List - UK Supermarkets
- **URL**: https://johnb.io/recipe-shopping-list
- **Summary**: Paste a recipe or meal plan and get one shopping list, grouped by aisle, with one-click search links for Tesco, Sainsbury's, Asda and 5 more.

### How It Works
1. Paste your recipes. One recipe or a week of them. An ingredients list is enough, but a full recipe with the method works too. If you want it scaled, write "double all of these" at the top and it will be handled.
2. Get one consolidated list. Ingredients are merged across recipes, quantities are added up, and everything is grouped into supermarket aisles in roughly the order you walk them.
3. Pick a shopping mode. Balanced, Premium pick or Best value. This rewrites the search term for every item instantly, with no waiting and no extra usage against your daily limit.
4. Choose your supermarket. The whole list re-links to whichever of the eight you select. Your choice is remembered for next time.
5. Work through the list. Each item opens that supermarket's search in a new tab, so your list stays put. Tick things off as you go; the ticks survive a page reload.
6. Or open them in bulk. The "Open all" button fires up a tab per remaining ingredient, ten at a time so your browser survives it. Ticked and hidden items are skipped. You will need to allow pop-ups for johnb.io the first time, and the button will tell you if your browser blocked them.

### Frequently Asked Questions
- **Q: Can it add everything to my basket automatically?**
  A: No, and be sceptical of anything that says it can. No UK supermarket offers a public add-to-basket API, so no website can fill your trolley without holding your login details. What this does is take you straight to the right search on your supermarket's own site, one ingredient at a time. You tap add, and they keep your basket.
- **Q: Which supermarkets does it work with?**
  A: Eight: Tesco, Sainsbury's, Asda, Morrisons, Ocado, Waitrose, Iceland and Co-op. Ocado results include M&S Food. You pick one supermarket at a time and the whole list re-links to it. Co-op is the weakest of the eight because its online shop is store-scoped, so it may ask for a postcode before running the search.
- **Q: What is the difference between the three shopping modes?**
  A: They change the words typed into the supermarket's search box, and nothing else. Balanced uses the plain product name. Premium pick adds qualifiers like free range or organic. Best value strips the term back so own-brand basics rank first. None of them changes what you pay, because you still choose the product yourself.
- **Q: Can I paste a whole week's meal plan?**
  A: Yes, and that is what it is built for. Ingredients appearing in more than one recipe are merged and their quantities added up, so three recipes needing onions produce one line telling you how many to buy. Each item shows which recipes it came from, so you can check nothing was missed.
- **Q: Does it work with American recipes?**
  A: Yes. US ingredient names are translated into UK supermarket vocabulary before the search links are built, so cilantro becomes coriander, zucchini becomes courgette and all-purpose flour becomes plain flour. Searching a UK supermarket for cilantro returns nothing at all, so this matters more than it sounds.
- **Q: Is it free, and is my recipe stored anywhere?**
  A: It is free, with a limit of three lists per day. There is no sign-up and nothing is kept on a server: your text goes to the AI, the list comes back, and that is the end of it. Ticked-off items are saved in your own browser only, so you can close the page mid-shop and pick up where you left off.

## Content Repurposer - One Post, Every Channel
- **URL**: https://johnb.io/content-repurposer
- **Summary**: Paste a blog post, article or press release and turn it into LinkedIn posts, X threads, Facebook copy, emails and video scripts with Claude AI.

### How It Works
1. Paste your content. The input accepts up to 10,000 characters - enough for a full blog post or article. The character counter updates as you type.
2. Select your platforms. Toggle which channels you want output for: LinkedIn, X, Facebook, Newsletter, 10-second video script or 30-second video script. Only selected platforms are generated, saving time and API usage. LinkedIn is selected by default.
3. Click Repurpose Content. Your selected content and platforms are sent to Claude Haiku. Each channel uses its own set of instructions - LinkedIn outputs are structured around a hook and professional tone; X outputs are condensed to fit character limits; newsletter outputs include a subject line; video scripts are written for spoken delivery with short, punchy sentences. The model does not simply summarise - it rewrites for each channel's conventions.
4. Review the outputs. Each channel appears in its own card with a word or character count badge. Always review before publishing - AI outputs may not fully match your brand voice, and factual details from the original should be checked for accuracy. The Writing Editor on JohnB.io can help refine tone and style before you publish.
5. Copy or share directly. Each card has a Copy button. LinkedIn and X cards also have direct Post buttons that open the platform with the text pre-filled (where supported by the platform).

### Frequently Asked Questions
- **Q: Which AI model does this tool use?**
  A: This tool uses Claude Haiku by Anthropic - the claude-haiku-5-5 model. Claude Haiku was chosen for its speed and cost efficiency for short-form content generation. Anthropic is an AI safety company; Claude is their primary large language model family.
- **Q: Is my content stored or used to train AI?**
  A: No - your content is not stored or used for AI training. It is sent to Anthropic's API solely to generate the outputs, then discarded. JohnB.io does not log or retain what you submit. See the Anthropic Privacy Policy for full details.
- **Q: Why is there a daily limit of 5 uses?**
  A: The tool allows 5 free uses per day per IP address without requiring a login. This keeps it accessible to everyone while preventing a single user from exhausting the daily API budget. The limit resets at midnight UTC. If you need higher-volume access, get in touch via LinkedIn .
- **Q: Why does the Facebook card not have a direct Post button?**
  A: Facebook removed support for pre-filling post text via share URLs since 2017 - this is a platform restriction, not a limitation of this tool. Use the Copy button to copy the text to your clipboard, then open Facebook and paste it into a new post.
- **Q: How long can my input content be?**
  A: The input accepts up to 10,000 characters - roughly 1,500–2,000 words, enough for a full blog post or article. For longer pieces, paste the most relevant section or a summary rather than the full text.
- **Q: What types of content work best with this tool?**
  A: Blog posts, articles, press releases and reports work best - structured long-form content with a clear point gives the AI more material to adapt. Very short inputs (under 100 words) may produce thin outputs. The tool is designed for content marketing use cases: turning existing written content into social and video-ready formats without rewriting from scratch. If you have a YouTube video, the JohnB.io Transcripts tool can extract the transcript first, which you can then paste here.
- **Q: What is the difference between content repurposing and content distribution?**
  A: Content distribution pushes the same piece of content to multiple channels without changing it - for example, sharing a blog post link on LinkedIn, X and Facebook simultaneously. Content repurposing adapts the source material into a different format and tone for each channel - the LinkedIn post leads with a professional hook, the X post is condensed to a punchy line, the newsletter has its own subject line. Distribution maximises reach; repurposing maximises relevance per platform.
- **Q: What are the limitations of AI-generated outputs?**
  A: AI outputs are a starting point, not a finished product. The model may not fully replicate your brand voice, may occasionally misrepresent a nuance in the original, and works best when the source material is clear and factual. Very technical or jargon-heavy content may produce generic outputs. Always review before publishing, verify any specific claims against the original, and add the personal context and voice that makes content distinctive. The tool is most effective for generating first drafts that you then edit, not copy-paste final outputs.

  A: Not reliably. If the AI rewrites significant portions of your text, those sections may be flagged by detectors such as GPTZero or Originality.ai . Review the output and rewrite anything that does not sound like you before publishing.

## LLM Chat
- **URL**: https://johnb.io/lm-chat
- **Summary**: Compare Claude, OpenAI and Gemini side by side in real time.

### How It Works
1. Chat with one model. Type a message in the input box under any of the three panels (Claude, OpenAI, Gemini) and press Enter or the send button. The model responds in that panel. Each panel maintains its own conversation thread, so you can continue a multi-turn dialogue with any one model independently.
2. Broadcast to all three. Type a prompt in the broadcast bar at the top and click Send to All. The same message is sent to all three models simultaneously and responses appear side by side, making it easy to compare how each model handles the same prompt.
3. Compare responses. Look across the three panels to see differences in tone, accuracy, length and reasoning. This is particularly useful for tasks like summarisation, creative writing, code generation or answering complex questions where model behaviour varies noticeably.
4. Continue the conversation. After a broadcast, you can follow up with each model individually. Each panel remembers its own prior turns, so you can dig deeper into a specific model's response without affecting the others.
5. Clear and reset. Use the delete button in the broadcast bar to clear all three conversations and start fresh.

### Frequently Asked Questions
- **Q: Which AI models are used?**
  A: The tool connects to three models: claude-sonnet-4-6 by Anthropic , gpt-4o-mini by OpenAI , and gemini-2.5-flash-lite by Google DeepMind . These are current production models as of August 2026.
- **Q: Are my messages stored?**
  A: Conversation history exists only in your browser for the current session and is cleared when you close the tab. Prompts are forwarded to each provider's API - they are subject to the respective privacy policies of Anthropic , OpenAI and Google . JohnB.io does not log or retain your messages.
- **Q: Why use GPT-4o-mini rather than GPT-4o?**
  A: GPT-4o-mini is a cost-efficient model that performs well for most conversational and reasoning tasks, making it a practical choice for a free comparison tool. For tasks requiring maximum capability from OpenAI, GPT-4o or GPT-o1 would be more appropriate - but those are better evaluated via ChatGPT directly.
- **Q: Can I use this to decide which model to use for my project?**
  A: Yes - this is one of the best use cases. Run your specific prompts through all three models and compare quality, speed and tone. Keep in mind that model performance varies by task type: coding, creative writing, factual Q&A and structured reasoning can produce noticeably different results across providers.
- **Q: Is there a usage limit?**
  A: There is no hard limit on the tool itself, but the underlying APIs have rate limits managed at the Cloudflare Worker level. If you hit a limit, wait a moment and try again. For high-volume testing, the best approach is to access the provider APIs directly with your own keys.

## Text to Voice
- **URL**: https://johnb.io/text-to-voice
- **Summary**: Convert text to voice with speed control and subtitle display.

### How It Works
1. Paste your text into the input area. The tool will display the word count and estimated reading and listening times as soon as you type or paste something.
2. Choose a voice. The Voice dropdown lists all speech synthesis voices installed on your device. The available voices vary by operating system and browser - Windows typically offers Microsoft voices, macOS offers Siri-based voices, and mobile devices have their own sets.
3. Set a playback speed. The Speed selector lets you choose from 0.8× (slower than natural pace) up to 1.75× (fast but still intelligible). 1.25× is the default - a good balance between pace and clarity for most content.
4. Click Start. The text begins playing. Each word is highlighted in the subtitle display below the control panel as it is spoken, making it easier to follow along or spot errors.
5. Use Pause and Stop as needed. Pause freezes playback at the current position. Stop ends playback entirely. Click Start again to restart from the beginning.

### Frequently Asked Questions
- **Q: Does this tool use AI?**
  A: No. The tool uses the Web Speech API , which is a standard browser feature - not a generative AI model. Speech synthesis is handled entirely by your browser and operating system. No AI model is called and no data is sent to any external service.
- **Q: Why does the Start button appear disabled when I first load the page?**
  A: The Start button is disabled until you enter some text. Once you paste or type in the input area, it activates automatically.
- **Q: Why are there no voices, or only one voice, in the dropdown?**
  A: Voice availability depends on your browser and operating system. Some browsers load voices asynchronously and the dropdown may appear empty on first load - try refreshing the page. On Windows, you can add more voices through Settings > Time & Language > Speech. On macOS, go to System Settings > Accessibility > Spoken Content.
- **Q: Does this work on mobile?**
  A: Yes. The Web Speech API is supported on iOS Safari and Android Chrome. Voice selection and quality vary by device and OS version. On iOS, the speech synthesis voices are the same ones used by VoiceOver and tend to sound natural.
- **Q: Is there a limit on how much text I can convert?**
  A: There is no limit set by this tool. In practice, some browsers impose internal limits on speech synthesis queue length. For very long documents, the tool may pause or stop mid-way in certain browsers. If this happens, split the text into smaller sections and play them separately.

## RAI Governance Framework
- **URL**: https://johnb.io/rai
- **Summary**: A responsible AI governance framework for evaluating and managing AI risk.

### How It Works
1. Classify your AI system. Use the Risk panel to run through the classification questionnaire. Answer questions about your system's domain, autonomy level, data use and potential impact. The tool assigns a risk tier - High, Medium or Low - with an explanation of what that means for your governance obligations.
2. Assign responsibility. In the Governance panel, populate the responsibility matrix with your team's roles. Define who is accountable for oversight, development, deployment and monitoring of each AI system.
3. Work through the checklist. The Checklist panel provides a structured set of pre-deployment checks covering fairness, explainability, data quality, human oversight and incident response. Mark items complete as you go.
4. Create a system card. The System Card panel generates a structured document recording your system's purpose, data sources, model type, identified risks, mitigations and oversight arrangements. Export it as a PDF or plain text file for your records.
5. Register and track systems. Add your AI systems to the Registry to maintain a searchable inventory. Use the Regulatory panel to map each system against relevant frameworks including the EU AI Act and UK AI principles.

### Frequently Asked Questions
- **Q: Does this tool use AI to generate the governance outputs?**
  A: No. All outputs - risk tier classifications, system cards, checklists and registry entries - are generated directly from the information you enter. There is no AI model involved. This is a structured documentation tool, not a generative AI tool.
- **Q: Is my data stored anywhere?**
  A: No. The tool runs entirely in your browser. Nothing is stored on any server, and nothing persists after you close the tab. If you want to keep your work, export it using the download options in each panel before closing.
- **Q: Which regulatory frameworks does the tool reference?**
  A: The risk classification aligns with the EU AI Act . The framework also references the UK government's AI Safety Institute principles, the ICO's AI and data protection guidance , and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework. It is intended as a practical starting point - always verify compliance requirements with qualified legal or regulatory counsel.
- **Q: What is a system card?**
  A: A system card (sometimes called a model card) is a structured document that records key facts about an AI system - its purpose, data sources, known risks, mitigations and human oversight arrangements. System cards are increasingly expected by regulators and enterprise procurement teams as part of responsible AI deployment. The original model card paper was published by Mitchell et al. at Google in 2018.
- **Q: Is this suitable for regulated industries?**
  A: The framework provides a solid foundation for AI governance in regulated industries including financial services, healthcare and the public sector. However, sector-specific requirements - such as those under the FCA's model risk guidance, NHS AI governance frameworks, or GDPR Article 22 on automated decision-making - may go beyond what this tool covers. Use it as a starting point and engage your compliance or legal team for sector-specific obligations.

## LLMs.txt Generator - Free AI-Ready Site Files
- **URL**: https://johnb.io/llms-generator
- **Summary**: Generate a structured llms.txt file from any URL or pasted content so ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Perplexity cite your website accurately.

### How It Works
1. Choose your input mode. Either enter your website URL (the tool fetches and analyses your homepage) or paste your content directly - for example a site description, list of pages, or an existing sitemap.
2. Click Generate. The content is sent to an AI model which reads it and produces a correctly structured llms.txt file following the llmstxt.org specification.
3. Review the output. The generated file will include a site title, a one-sentence description, and logically grouped sections with descriptions for each page or resource.
4. Copy or download. Use the Copy button to grab the text, or Download to save it directly as llms.txt .
5. Upload to your site root. Place the file at yourdomain.com/llms.txt so that AI systems can find it automatically. No code changes required.

### Frequently Asked Questions
- **Q: What is an llms.txt file?**
  A: An llms.txt file is a plain text file placed at the root of a website that provides a concise, structured overview of the site's content formatted for large language models. It was proposed by Jeremy Howard (fast.ai) in September 2024 and is defined at llmstxt.org. It follows a simple format: a site title, a one-sentence description, and sections listing pages with brief descriptions.
- **Q: Does llms.txt help with Google SEO rankings?**
  A: Not directly. Google's organic search rankings are based on its own crawl and indexing signals. However, llms.txt is important for GEO (Generative Engine Optimisation) - helping AI assistants like ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google's AI Overviews understand and accurately cite your content. As AI-generated answers increasingly influence how users find information, GEO is becoming an important complement to traditional SEO.
- **Q: Which AI systems read llms.txt?**
  A: AI assistants with live web access - including ChatGPT (with browsing), Perplexity AI, Claude (with web access), and Bing Copilot - can retrieve and read llms.txt during inference. Some AI training datasets and indexing pipelines also process llms.txt to understand site structure. Cloudflare supports the format natively as of 2025.
- **Q: Is llms.txt the same as robots.txt or sitemap.xml?**
  A: No. Robots.txt controls which pages web crawlers can access. Sitemap.xml lists all URLs for search engine indexing. Llms.txt is a separate, human- and machine-readable summary specifically designed to help LLMs understand what your site is about and identify its most important pages. All three can and should coexist.
- **Q: What should I include in my llms.txt?**
  A: At minimum: your site name, a one-sentence description, and a list of your most important pages with brief descriptions of what each contains. Group pages into logical sections (e.g. Tools, Blog, About, Documentation). The goal is to give an LLM a clear mental model of your site in under two minutes of reading.
- **Q: How often should I update my llms.txt?**
  A: Update it whenever you add significant new content, launch new pages or tools, or change the focus of your site. For most sites, reviewing it quarterly is sufficient. Treat it like your sitemap - keep it current but not obsessively maintained.
- **Q: Can this tool generate llms.txt for any website?**
  A: The URL mode fetches and analyses your homepage. It works best on content-rich pages with clear headings and descriptions. Some sites may block automated fetches - if that happens, use Paste Content mode and provide a description of your site manually.

## FAQ Schema Generator - Free JSON-LD FAQPage Tool
- **URL**: https://johnb.io/faq-schema
- **Summary**: Generate valid FAQPage JSON-LD structured data from question and answer pairs. Manual builder plus AI draft mode, ready to paste into your HTML head.

### How It Works
1. Pick your mode. Write Manually if you already have the questions. Draft with AI if you want a first pass from a topic.
2. Fill in Q&As. Add as many question and answer pairs as you need. You can remove any row.
3. Click Generate. The tool outputs a complete FAQPage JSON-LD block following Schema.org guidelines.
4. Copy the output. Use the Copy button to grab the full script tag, ready to paste.
5. Paste into your head. Drop it inside the <head> of your page. Make sure the visible page content has the same questions and answers.
6. Validate. Run the page through Google Rich Results Test to confirm the schema parses cleanly.

### Frequently Asked Questions
- **Q: What is FAQPage schema?**
  A: FAQPage is a Schema.org type that marks up a page containing a list of questions and answers. Search engines use it to understand the content structure, and in some cases display rich results that show the questions directly in search listings.
- **Q: Does Google still show FAQ rich results?**
  A: Since August 2023 Google has limited FAQ rich results to a small set of well-known government and health sites. The schema is still worth adding because it helps AI assistants and other search engines understand the page, and it costs nothing to include.
- **Q: Where do I paste the generated code?**
  A: Paste it inside a script tag with type application/ld+json in the head section of the page. The questions and answers in the schema must match the visible content on the page, otherwise Google treats it as a violation of its structured data guidelines.
- **Q: Can I generate FAQs from a topic?**
  A: Yes. The Draft with AI tab takes a topic or a URL and returns five to eight relevant questions and answers. Review the output before publishing to make sure it is accurate and matches the page content.
- **Q: Is the output valid JSON-LD?**
  A: The tool outputs FAQPage JSON-LD that follows Schema.org and Google structured data guidelines. You can validate the result in Google Rich Results Test or Schema.org Validator before publishing.

- **Q: Can I print the merged PDF directly?**

### Frequently Asked Questions

- **Q: What is the difference between EU-wide and country-specific regulations?**
  A: EU-wide regulations - such as GDPR, the AML directives, PSD2, the AI Act, and the Digital Services Act - apply across all EU and/or EEA member states either directly or through national transposition. Country-specific regulations apply to operators licensed in or targeting users in that particular jurisdiction. Most EU-licensed iGaming operators face both layers simultaneously.
- **Q: What are the biggest iGaming regulatory changes in 2024 to 2026?**
  A: The most consequential changes are: Ireland's Gambling Regulation Act 2024 (GRAI B2C betting licence applications opened February 2026); the EU AML Package including the new AMLA authority and the 2024 AML Regulation (effective July 2027); Brazil's SPA licensing regime (fully operational January 2025); Curaçao's LOK reform replacing the master/sublicence system (December 2024); India's Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act 2025; and Kenya's Gambling Control Act 2025. See the Key Developments section on this page for full details on all ten major changes.
- **Q: Does the map cover every iGaming regulation or only the major ones?**
  A: The database tracks all significant regulations, directives, and licensing frameworks that an iGaming compliance officer would need to monitor - including gambling-specific acts, AML obligations, data protection laws, payment services rules, digital services regulations, advertising codes, and international testing standards such as GLI and eCOGRA. ## iGaming Bonus Cost Calculator
- **URL**: https://johnb.io/bonus-calculator
- **Summary**: Calculate the true operator cost of casino bonuses. Enter bonus amount, wagering requirement, house edge and completion rate for net cost analysis.

### How It Works
1. Enter the bonus amount. This is the monetary value credited to the player - for example, a 100% match bonus on a £100 deposit gives a £100 bonus.
2. Set the wagering requirement. The multiplier applied to the bonus before it can be withdrawn. A 35× requirement on a £100 bonus means the player must wager £3,500 in total.
3. Enter the house edge. The percentage of each bet the operator retains on average over the long run. Slots typically range from 3% to 6%. Live blackjack can be under 1%. The game mix that qualifies for wagering significantly affects cost.
4. Set the player completion rate. The percentage of bonus recipients who complete the full wagering requirement and claim the bonus. Industry averages vary widely - typical ranges are 40% to 70% depending on the offer structure and player segment.
5. Click Calculate. The tool returns your four key metrics and a scenario table showing how cost shifts at different completion rates.

### Frequently Asked Questions
- **Q: What is a wagering requirement in iGaming?**
  A: A wagering requirement (also called a playthrough requirement) is the number of times a player must bet the bonus amount before it converts to withdrawable cash. A 35× requirement on a £100 bonus means the player must place £3,500 of bets. The higher the multiplier, the more the operator expects to recoup from the player's losses before the bonus is released.
- **Q: What is a typical house edge for slot games?**
  A: Most online slots operate between 94% and 97% RTP (Return to Player), which translates to a 3% to 6% house edge. Premium branded slots or progressive jackpot titles sometimes carry a higher house edge of 7–10%. Live dealer games like blackjack (with basic strategy) have edges below 1%, which is why many operators either restrict table game contributions or require higher wagering multipliers.
- **Q: What is a realistic player completion rate?**
  A: Completion rates depend heavily on the offer structure, player segment and wagering requirement level. Welcome bonuses with 30–40× requirements typically see completion rates between 40% and 65%. High wagering requirements (50×+) or restricted game selections can push completion below 30%. Free spin bonuses often have lower absolute completion rates since the bonus value is lower. The default of 60% in this tool is a reasonable mid-market estimate.
- **Q: How is the breakeven house edge calculated?**
  A: The breakeven occurs when expected player losses equal the bonus amount. If a player wagers B × W total, they lose B × W × HE on average. Setting this equal to the bonus B: B × W × HE = B, so HE = 1 ÷ W. At 35× wagering, the breakeven house edge is 1 ÷ 35 = 2.86%. Any game with a house edge above this is profitable for the operator from completing players.
- **Q: Does this tool comply with UK Gambling Commission bonus advertising rules?**
  A: This is a cost-modelling tool for operators and is not a consumer-facing bonus advertisement. It does not claim any specific bonus offer exists or is available. For guidance on compliant bonus advertising under UKGC rules, refer to the UKGC Licence Conditions and Codes of Practice and the ASA Non-Broadcast Advertising Code .

- **URL**: https://johnb.io/tcs-simplifier

### Frequently Asked Questions
- **Q: What does the T&Cs Simplifier do?**
  A: It takes the full terms and conditions of a casino bonus offer and produces a short plain English summary plus a red flag list. The red flags cover things like high wagering requirements, short expiry windows, game weighting restrictions and maximum cashout limits.
- **Q: Is this tool legal advice?**
  A: No. This is an informational tool designed to make bonus terms easier to read. It is not legal or financial advice and it does not replace a compliance review. Always check the original terms on the operator site before accepting a bonus.

  A: Players who want to understand what they are signing up for, affiliates writing honest reviews of bonus offers, and compliance teams checking that promotional terms are clear and not misleading.
- **Q: What counts as a red flag?**
  A: Typical red flags are wagering requirements above 35x, expiry windows under 7 days, game weightings that exclude popular titles, maximum win caps, and clauses that let the operator void winnings at their discretion.
- **Q: Does the tool store the terms I paste?**
  A: No. The pasted text is sent to a Cloudflare Worker that forwards it to an AI model and returns the summary. Nothing is logged or saved beyond standard rate limit counters tied to your IP.

## Football 2026 - AI Tournament Simulator
- **URL**: https://johnb.io/football-2026
- **Summary**: AI predictions and interactive simulator for the Summer 2026 football tournament. Group tables, 48-team ratings and clickable knockout bracket.

### How It Works
1. Squad data built for all 48 teams. Each team has a squad rating (0-100), a form score based on their last 5 matches, a coach rating, and 8 key players — each rated individually for overall quality and current form.
2. Group stage simulated. All 6 fixtures per group are run using head-to-head probability weighting from the squad and form data. The top 2 from each group advance to the knockout rounds.
3. Knockout bracket generated. Teams are seeded by group finish and paired into the Round of 32. Each subsequent round simulates match probabilities using the same model — winner advances, loser exits.
4. Win probability calculated. The AI runs the full bracket and assigns each team a tournament win percentage based on their likely path, squad strength, and form at each stage. Argentina's 18% reflects their depth across all three phases.
5. Click to change any result. Click any team in the knockout bracket to make them the winner of that match. The bracket updates automatically from that point forward through all later rounds.
6. Reset at any time. The reset button restores the original AI prediction across all rounds instantly.

### Frequently Asked Questions
- **Q: Why are you not calling the tournament by its real name?**
  A: The short answer is money and incredibly strict trademark laws. When you see a website, brand, or merchandise seller avoiding the name (or the official branding), it is almost always to avoid being sued by their legal team.
- **Q: Is this betting advice?**
  A: Absolutely not. This is an AI prediction — I would not suggest betting on this outcome.
- **Q: How does the AI produce the predictions? What data does it use?**
  A: It reviewed 5 international matches per team and assessed 8 key players per squad, using training data and web searches to make informed qualitative judgements, not live statistical feeds.
- **Q: How does the Football 2026 simulator work?**
  A: The simulator uses a deep analysis of all 48 teams based on squad ratings, coach quality, recent form, and tournament history. AI predicts group stage results and generates a full knockout bracket. You can click any team in the bracket to override the prediction and see how the tournament path changes.
- **Q: Which team does the AI predict to win?**
  A: The AI predicts Argentina to win the Summer 2026 tournament, with France and Spain as the closest challengers. Argentina's 18% probability reflects their defending champion status, the Messi factor, and the deepest midfield in the tournament.
- **Q: How are the team and player ratings calculated?**
  A: Ratings are on a 0-100 scale based on current club form, international performance, and squad depth. World Class (88+) covers generational players. Elite (80-87) covers top-level internationals. Good (72-79) covers solid squad contributors. Below 72 is squad depth.
- **Q: Can I change the bracket results?**
  A: Yes. Click any team button in the knockout bracket to make them the winner of that match. The change cascades forward automatically through all later rounds. Click Reset to go back to the AI prediction.
- **Q: How many teams are in the 2026 tournament?**
  A: 48 teams compete across 12 groups of 4. Two teams advance from each group, giving 24 teams in the Round of 32 plus 8 third-place qualifiers. The knockout rounds are: Round of 32, Round of 16, Quarter-finals, Semi-finals, and the Final.

## Profit Calculator
- **URL**: https://johnb.io/ebay
- **Summary**: eBay and Vinted profit calculator for resellers.

### How It Works
1. Choose a tab. Select Vinted, eBay or Saleroom depending on where you bought or plan to sell your items. Each tab has fee settings specific to that platform.
2. Add your items. For Vinted and saleroom lots, you can paste listing HTML or enter items manually. For eBay, enter your sale price, purchase cost and postage. Set a default postage cost to apply it across multiple items at once.
3. Adjust fee rates. The tool pre-fills with current standard rates - eBay final value fee (default 13%), Vinted buyer protection, saleroom buyer's premium and online commission. Update these if your account has negotiated rates or if platform rates have changed.
4. Review your profit summary. The tool displays profit per item, total profit across all items, ROI percentage and a suggested minimum sale price to hit your target profit margin. Use the filter to show only profitable items or high-return items.
5. Sort and export. Sort columns by any field - sale price, profit, ROI. Your data is automatically saved to localStorage and reloads the next time you open the tool.

### Frequently Asked Questions
- **Q: What is eBay's current final value fee?**
  A: eBay's standard final value fee for most private sellers in the UK is around 12.8–13.2% of the total sale amount including postage, as of March 2026. This varies by category - vehicles, property and business equipment have different rates. Always check eBay's current fee schedule before relying on this tool's default. eBay also charges a per-transaction fee of £0.30 for private sellers, which this tool accounts for separately.
- **Q: Does Vinted charge selling fees?**
  A: Vinted does not charge the seller a commission - instead it charges a buyer protection fee to the buyer. This means your sale price is what you receive (minus postage if you are covering it). However, Vinted's fee structure does include optional promoted listing fees and postage labels purchased through the platform.
- **Q: What is a buyer's premium in a saleroom context?**
  A: A buyer's premium is a percentage added to the hammer price at auction, paid by the buyer. For resellers who buy at auction and sell on eBay or Vinted, the total cost of an item is the hammer price plus the buyer's premium (typically 20–30%), plus any applicable VAT on the premium. The saleroom tab in this tool lets you enter the buyer's premium percentage and any online commission charged by the auction platform.
- **Q: Will my data be lost if I clear my browser cache?**
  A: Yes. The tool saves to localStorage, which is cleared when you clear site data or browser storage. If you have important item lists, export or note them down before clearing your cache.
- **Q: Does this tool use AI?**
  A: No. All profit calculations are straightforward arithmetic based on the values you enter. There is no AI model involved and no data is sent to any external service.

## Bill Calculator
- **URL**: https://johnb.io/calculator
- **Summary**: Use JohnB.io's Bill Calculator to split bills and calculate tips easily.

### How It Works
1. Enter the total bill amount in pounds. This is the full amount before tip - what the restaurant is charging.
2. Set a tip percentage. Common amounts are 10% (standard), 12.5% (often added automatically in London restaurants) and 15% (generous). Enter 0 for no tip.
3. Enter the number of people splitting the bill. For a solo diner, leave this at 1.
4. Click Calculate. The tool instantly returns the tip amount, the total bill with tip included, and the amount each person owes.

### Frequently Asked Questions
- **Q: Does this tool use AI?**
  A: No. This is a straightforward arithmetic calculator. There is no AI model involved - the calculations are simple maths run locally in your browser using Pyodide.
- **Q: What is Pyodide?**
  A: Pyodide is a version of Python compiled to WebAssembly that runs directly in web browsers. It allows Python code to execute client-side without a server, which is what powers the calculation logic here.
- **Q: What tip percentage should I leave in the UK?**
  A: In the UK, 10–15% is standard for sit-down restaurants where service is not already included. Many London restaurants add a 12.5% service charge automatically - check your bill before adding more. Tipping is discretionary; you are not obligated to pay a tip that has been added without your agreement. Which? has clear guidance on service charges and your rights.
- **Q: Does the split have to be equal?**
  A: This calculator assumes an equal split between all diners. For unequal splits - where each person pays for what they ordered - you would need to calculate each person's portion separately and enter it as a solo bill.
- **Q: Is my data stored?**
  A: No. The tool stores nothing. Your bill amount and settings exist only in the page for the duration of your visit and are not transmitted anywhere.

- **Summary**: Evaluate your poker experience and plan your game strategy.

### Frequently Asked Questions
- **Q: Is this tool connected to any poker site or gambling operator?**
  A: No. This tool has no affiliation with any gambling operator and receives no commission from any poker site. It is a standalone information tool built for entertainment purposes.
- **Q: How many buy-ins should I have for a given stake?**
  A: A standard recreational bankroll guideline is 20–30 buy-ins for cash games and 50–100 buy-ins for tournaments, due to higher variance. For example, a £50 bankroll is only suitable for micro-stakes games (£0.01/£0.02 blinds or £1–£2 buy-in tournaments). Playing higher stakes with fewer buy-ins significantly increases your risk of going broke through normal variance.
- **Q: I think I may have a gambling problem. Where can I get help?**
  A: Free, confidential support is available 24 hours a day in the UK: GambleAware - 0808 8020 133 (free, 24/7); GamCare National Helpline - 0808 8020 133; Gambling Therapy - free online support worldwide; GAMSTOP - free self-exclusion from all UK-licensed online gambling sites.
- **Q: What is the difference between online and live poker bankroll requirements?**
  A: Online poker tends to require a larger bankroll relative to stakes because hands are dealt faster, meaning variance plays out more quickly. Live poker has a slower pace and often softer competition at low stakes, but travel and time costs add up. This tool accounts for your experience type when making recommendations.
- **Q: Does this tool store my budget information?**
  A: No. The tool stores nothing. Your budget input and answers exist only in the page for the duration of your visit and are not transmitted to any server.

## Zig-Zag Drop Mystery
- **URL**: https://johnb.io/zzmystery
- **Summary**: Zig-Zag Drop Mystery: a free browser plinko-style slot demo. Drop the ball, watch it bounce, no signup and no real money involved.

### How It Works
1. Set your virtual bet amount using the +/− buttons or the slider. The default is 2.00 virtual points. This is not real money - it is just a number used to calculate virtual winnings relative to your stake.
2. Choose a risk level. Low risk gives more frequent small wins. High risk gives rare large multipliers with more frequent losses. Medium is a balance between the two.
3. Select the number of rows. More rows means more pegs and a wider spread of possible landing slots, generally producing a tighter distribution of outcomes.
4. Pick a ball count. You can drop 1 to 100 balls per round. More balls give a better sense of the overall probability distribution in a single run.
5. Click BET to drop the balls. Watch them bounce through the pegs and land in multiplier slots. Your virtual balance updates based on the outcomes. Enable auto-bet to run rounds continuously.

### Frequently Asked Questions
- **Q: Is this real gambling?**
  A: No. This game uses virtual points only. There is no real money involved, no way to deposit funds and no way to withdraw winnings. It is a browser-based coding project inspired by Plinko mechanics, built purely for fun.
- **Q: Why include responsible gambling information if it is not real gambling?**
  A: Because the game closely resembles real-money gambling products. The mechanics - variable rewards, fast pace, risk settings - are the same as those found in regulated gambling products. Anyone who finds themselves strongly drawn to this type of game should be aware of the risks before playing real-money versions.
- **Q: What is the house edge in this game?**
  A: Like real Plinko-style casino games, the multiplier values are set so that the expected return is less than 1.0x your stake over a large number of rounds. At High risk, the rare high multipliers are not frequent enough to overcome the common low-multiplier outcomes. This is intentional - it mirrors how real casino games work to ensure the house has an edge.
- **Q: Where can I get help if I have a gambling problem?**
  A: Free, confidential help is available 24/7 in the UK: GambleAware - 0808 8020 133; GamCare National Helpline - 0808 8020 133; Gambling Therapy - free online support worldwide; GAMSTOP - self-exclude from all UK-licensed gambling sites for free.
- **Q: What is the Galton board connection?**
  A: A Galton board (also called a bean machine or quincunx) is a statistical demonstration device invented by Sir Francis Galton. Balls dropped through rows of pegs produce a binomial distribution - the same physical principle that Plinko-style games are based on. This game is partly a visual illustration of that probability concept.
